classifiedFindings.title: setRoute validates the last non-zero path entry, but Curve Router NG stops at the first empty pool slot, so a gapped route is accepted and silently strands the intermediate token
classifiedFindings.label: M-01

classification.assetImpact: The caller's paid-for yield on the gap-routed strategy is lost, every harvest. SYA is paid in full for that strategy's yield, the router delivers the intermediate token (crvUSD on fork) instead of the reward token, and the intermediate is held by the harvester. It is not a strategy token, so _sellYield never touches it, and there is no sweep (DEDUP-007), so it is stuck permanently. CORRECTION to the brief: the stranded value is NOT claimable by the next caller in the proven case. Only if the intermediate happened to be another routed strategy token would a later harvest sell it, which moves the value to an unrelated caller rather than recovering it. Protocol (SYA) value is not at risk; the loss falls on harvest callers, a permissionless set that includes third parties.
attackPath: 1. Precondition (non-obvious owner footgun): the owner registers a multi-hop route in which a middle pool/token slot is address(0), e.g. a two-hop USDe->crvUSD->USDC route whose second pool address resolved to zero, with USDC in a later slot. setRoute's validator, which is advertised (and prescribed by story-001) as the route-end guard, accepts it because USDC is the last non-zero entry.
2. Any caller (harvest.sh or a third party) calls harvest(). Curve Router NG stops at the first empty pool slot and delivers crvUSD, not USDC (fork: 100 USDe -> 100.09 crvUSD, 0 USDC).

3. Proceeds from the other strategies (or the 1% buffer, or a USDe-exempt-free claim with reward-token yield) cover `owed`, so the underflow guard at L284 does not fire; the harvest succeeds (fork: 'harvest ok true', 4.29e18 crvUSD stranded).
4. harvest.sh derives minEthOut from an eth_call simulation that already reflects the strand, so the caller's only slippage protection does not catch it. Nothing reverts and no event flags it.
5. Repeats on every harvest until the route is noticed and fixed; each round's stranded tokens are permanent.
classification.likelihood: medium - requires a single owner configuration slip (a zero middle slot) that the validator was specifically supposed to reject; once present, loss is certain and recurring with no further action. Halmos A3 proves the gap is the ONLY silent-misroute shape, so the hazard is narrow but real.
classification.assumptions: Owner is non-malicious and mis-enters a route with a middle zero slot (typo / unset address variable / slot-10 convention). Other proceeds cover the borrow (otherwise it fails loud).
classification.externalRequirements: Owner route-registration slip; at least one other harvested strategy or reward-token yield covering owed.

classifiedFindings.justification: Resolved flagged question 1 as MEDIUM (operational hazard / owner footgun). Law 3 test: a competent non-malicious owner who sees setRoute reject a wrong route end would be surprised that a route with a missing middle hop passes and then silently pays the router output into a dead balance. The consequence is not obvious, so this is a footgun, not trusted misuse, and is classified by the impact it unlocks. That impact is real-value loss (the caller pays SYA the discounted price for yield it never receives), silent (the harvest succeeds and simulation-derived minEthOut absorbs it), recurring (every harvest), and permanent (no sweep, not a strategy token). That matches C4 Medium 'leak value with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements'; the stated assumption is the owner slip. Not High: it needs the owner precondition, the loss is per-harvest bounded by one strategy's yield, protocol/SYA funds are untouched, and no attacker profits. Not Low: the validator was the designed guard against exactly this, the story's own rule is the root cause (F-02, story-unsafe), story-002's 'zero balances after a successful harvest' acceptance and CLAUDE.md's 'reverts rather than stranding' invariant are both broken, and the harm reaches third-party callers rather than staying with the owner. Fork PoC, adversarial invariants on forge+medusa, and Halmos witnesses all agree. Flagged for severity-auditor second opinion as a footgun-gated Medium; floor is Low.
classifiedFindings.safeConfigGuidance: Until fixed: after every setRoute, read getRoute(token) and confirm path[2k] for the first k with path[2k+1]==0 equals sya.rewardToken() and every later slot is zero; also eth_call the router with the stored route and check the output token. Fix: contiguity check in setRoute (Halmos A5/A6 prove it sufficient and non-rejecting), amend story-001's rule, make MockCurveRouter follow Router NG semantics.

classifiedFindings.title: _sellYield acts on the raw token balance, so 1-wei donations (or a strategy's own sub-dust delivery) brick every harvest
classifiedFindings.label: L-01

classification.assetImpact: None. Harvest reverts atomically; the unharvested yield stays in the strategies and SYA pays it out on a later claim.
attackPath: Natural (no adversary, fails in the HONEST invariant config): a non-exempt strategy delivers a sub-router-threshold amount (e.g. 298075 wei USDe); Router NG reverts 'Received nothing' and the whole harvest reverts.
Griefer: any EOA donates 1 wei of a strategy token whose strategy delivers 0 this round (routed -> router dust revert; unrouted -> RouteNotConfigured).
Caller workaround in the same block: add that strategy to exemptStrategies (exempt tokens are skipped by _sellYield).
classification.likelihood: high - occurs naturally with no attacker
classification.externalRequirements: A strategy that delivers dust/zero in the round being harvested.

classifiedFindings.justification: The honest-config failure raises likelihood (this will happen in normal operation, not only under griefing), which rules out QA/Info and puts it at the top of Low. It does not raise impact: no value is at risk, the revert is atomic, and the caller has a per-call parameter workaround (exempt the strategy), so this is availability friction on a stateless helper rather than impaired protocol function. SYA's own claim path is unaffected. The workaround is degraded by L-04 (the operator script cannot name the offending token), which is recorded there rather than inflating this finding. Faithful to story-002 Flow step 5, whose balance-based rule is the root (F-03).

classifiedFindings.title: Neither the on-chain Unprofitable check nor harvest.sh's minEthOut floor prices the claim NFT burned by SYA; default config sends net-loss harvests
classifiedFindings.label: L-02

classification.assetImpact: Caller self-loss of up to about one claim-NFT mint price per harvest (index 1 ~10.78 USD) when the shipped harvest.sh default (MIN_PROFIT_WEI=0) sends harvests whose ETH out covers gas but not the NFT burned. No third party extracts value; protocol unaffected.
attackPath: Not an attack: operator runs harvest.sh with defaults; the floor prices gas only; a harvest netting less than the NFT's value is sent (story-005's own anvil run nets ~-2.2 USD).
classification.assumptions: Caller values the burned NFT at its mint price.

classifiedFindings.justification: Real but self-inflicted and parameter-controlled loss to the operator using its own tool, with no attacker and no protocol impact. C4 places caller-side economics with a configurable floor in QA/Low. Kept at Low (not QA) because the shipped default systematically sends net-loss transactions and the project's own Purpose definition of 'profitable' (> gas + NFT cost) is violated; the spec contradicts itself, so F-01 goes to spec-conformance for the owner to reconcile.

classifiedFindings.title: Routes and ethPool are validated against sya.rewardToken() only at set time; an SYA setRewardToken bricks harvest and the harvester owner cannot pre-stage the new config
classifiedFindings.label: L-03

classification.assetImpact: None. Fail-loud harvest outage between SYA's setRewardToken and the harvester owner re-registering routes/ethPool.
attackPath: SYA owner switches rewardToken; every harvest reverts (fork: WrappedError 0x90bfb865); the harvester owner cannot pre-stage the new config (rejected before the switch, old config rejected after).
classification.likelihood: low - requires a rare cross-owner migration

classifiedFindings.justification: Cross-owner footgun (a competent owner would expect to pre-stage), but the impact it unlocks is only a temporary, loud availability gap on a helper contract, with no value at risk and recovery by an ordinary owner call. Low with runbook guidance. Distinct root from SYA M-02 (sya14m02, fixed).
classifiedFindings.safeConfigGuidance: Put 'clear and re-register harvester routes + ethPool immediately after setRewardToken' in the SYA reward-token migration runbook.

classifiedFindings.label: L-04
classifiedFindings.title: harvest.sh cannot decode SYA, strategy, oracle or Router NG reverts, so the operator cannot tell which strategy to exempt (story-005 'readable reason on any simulated revert' unmet)

classification.assetImpact: None directly; abort-before-send still holds. It removes the operator's means of applying the L-01 workaround: ZeroAmount, NoValidNFT, ExemptStrategyNotRegistered, EnforcedPause, Tokemak InvalidDataReturned print as raw selectors, and Router NG dust reverts print empty data with no token named.
attackPath: Operator runs harvest.sh; the simulation reverts on a strategy-side or router-dust error (L-01 occurs naturally); the script prints a bare selector or nothing; the operator has to guess which strategy to exempt, so harvesting stalls.
classification.likelihood: high - pairs with L-01's natural trigger
classification.assumptions: Operator relies on harvest.sh as shipped.

classifiedFindings.justification: Resolved flagged question 3 as LOW, split out of the DEDUP-011 bundle. It is not tooling cosmetics. It is an unmet story-005 acceptance criterion (Law 2, F-05), and it is the one thing standing between L-01's natural DoS and its documented workaround, so it has availability consequence. It is not higher than Low because no value is at risk and the transaction is never sent on revert. It gets its own fingerprint so a fix to decode_revert can be reconciled independently of the remaining QA residuals (a, b, d), which keep the parent fingerprint.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Add the SYA/strategy/oracle selectors to KNOWN_ERRORS; on empty revert data, re-simulate with each strategy exempted in turn (or call sya.getYield per strategy) and name the offending token.

classifiedFindings.title: Borrow/allowance = calculateClaimAmount*1.01 with a false '~10% over-estimate' premise; DOLA runs with only 1% headroom, and over-delivery beyond it reverts the claim
classifiedFindings.label: Q-01
classifiedFindings.justification: Resolved flagged question 2 as QA/Info, not Low. The revert path needs a strategy that delivers more than its own same-transaction calculateClaimAmount estimate by >1%. No live strategy does: fork measurements show paid/estimate of 99.00% (USDC), 75.12% (USDe), 100.00% (DOLA), all at or below the estimate. The DOLA-only sharpening shows the headroom shrinks to exactly 1% when others are exempted, but headroom is only consumed by over-delivery, which is unobserved on live code; the invariant failures used a synthetic +2-3% over-delivering double. Impact even then is a loud atomic revert with no loss. What is real is the false '~10% over-estimate, safe direction' premise in story-002 and NatSpec L265-268; it is routed to spec-conformance as F-04 so the owner sees it, and becomes Low if SYA ever adds a strategy whose delivery can exceed its estimate. The SYMBOLIC-002 sub-observation (buffer floors to 0 below 100 units) is dust.

classifiedFindings.title: Exact-input V4 swap with sqrtPriceLimitX96 = MAX-1 can partially fill, leaving the unswapped reward token for the next caller
classifiedFindings.label: Q-02
classifiedFindings.justification: Partial fill of the exact-input V4 swap is unreachable on the configured 0.3% ETH/USDC pool at harvest sizes, and the caller is protected by minEthOut. Hardening note only.

classifiedFindings.title: No rescue path: stray non-strategy ERC20s and ERC1155 ids are stuck forever; stray strategy tokens/reward/ETH are swept to the next caller via whole-balance logic
classifiedFindings.label: Q-03
classifiedFindings.justification: No rescue path for mistakenly-sent tokens. The 'pot theft' premise was refuted (no path lets a non-caller take an honest caller's ETH). Kept as QA; it is the aggravator that makes M-01's strand permanent, so the M-01 fix should include a sweep.

classifiedFindings.title: Single aggregate slippage bound: intermediate legs run with minOut 0 / no price limit, harvest() has no deadline and accepts minEthOut=0; MEV exposure if the private relay leaks
classifiedFindings.label: Q-04
classifiedFindings.justification: Single end-to-end minEthOut bound is a documented design decision; exposure is caller-only and sub-dollar at current sizes, and a public-mempool leak needs the operator to bypass the private relay. A direct caller passing minEthOut=0 is user input. Deadline sub-issue counted once under Q-07.

classifiedFindings.title: Documented 'double fee' mechanism on USDe/crvUSD pool 0xF55B is wrong (opposite-direction trades, not adverse price move); direct USDe/USDC route avoids the round trip
classifiedFindings.label: Q-05
classifiedFindings.justification: Wrong mechanism in the story-004/MainnetRoutes comment ('double fee'), costing cents per harvest; a route-choice and documentation note for the caller's economics. No security impact.

classifiedFindings.title: Test-suite fidelity gaps hide DEDUP-001 and DEDUP-005 regressions
classifiedFindings.label: Q-06
classifiedFindings.justification: Test-suite fidelity gaps (vacuous test_noHarvestFunction, MockCurveRouter copying the harvester's last-non-zero rule, MockSYA never over-delivering). Non-security in itself, but the MockCurveRouter gap is why M-01 is invisible to the unit suite, so it should ride with the M-01 fix.

classifiedFindings.title: Operator script (script/harvest.sh) residuals: no deadline, cast-send timeout re-run, PRIVATE_RPC_URL not verified private
classifiedFindings.proposedSeverityUpstream: QA (sub-issue c may be Low as a story-005 conformance gap)
classifiedFindings.label: Q-07
classifiedFindings.justification: Remaining residuals are operator-hardening only: minEthOut binds regardless of inclusion delay (a), a re-run after a send timeout costs only gas on a revert (b), and relay choice is the operator's (d). End-to-end script maths was verified sound. Keeps the parent fingerprint; sub-issue (c) split to L-04 with its own fingerprint.
